Subject: Security exhibit clarification and evidence cadence request

Hi Markus,

Thanks for sending the redlined MSA + order form. Our legal team reviewed the security exhibit and has three items they want to clarify before we proceed:

1) Penetration testing window: our default procurement policy requires a 6–8 week notice and a staging window with scoped IP ranges. The draft language seems to imply on-demand access. Can you confirm preservation of the staging carveout?

2) Evidence cadence: we need a quarterly evidence cadence for SOC 2 artifacts plus a 30-day response SLA for ad-hoc evidence requests. The MSA references "reasonable" response times. Can Redwood commit to a 30-day SLA and provide a primary evidence contact?

3) Data isolation for dedicated instances: please confirm whether the order form footprint for our instance is single-tenant (we asked for dedicated capacity).

We have a planned procurement review meeting on 10/30 and would love to get a redline back by EOD 10/25 if possible. Attaching our procurement checklist for reference.

Appreciate the help — happy to jump on a short call if easier.

Thanks,
Arjun
Procurement Manager, Coventis Health

Proposed:
- Pen-test: preserve staging carveout and require 14-day notice for production-affecting tests, agree to 6–8 week scheduling window for larger tests. Redwood offers a 48-hour read-only snapshot for non-destructive scans.
- Evidence SLA: commit to 30-day response for standard SOC 2 artifacts and 10 business days for ticketed requests labeled as "procurement evidence". Escalation path to Ben for missed SLAs.
- Dedicated capacity: confirm order form already specifies Dedicated pool and tenancy; legal may want an explicit sentence about single-tenant isolation and data separation controls.

Ben — can you weigh in on the pen-test IP scoping and the snapshot capability? Laura/Karthik — any redline language you want me to push back to them with?

—Markus

Markus/Laura — quick notes from infra/security:

- Pen-test windows: 14 days notice for production is reasonable; for full-scope penetration tests that require access to staging we typically ask for 6 weeks to coordinate engineering and monitoring. We'll agree to a 6–8 week scheduling window when the test requires more than 1 FTE of engineering support.
- IP scoping: we can provide ephemeral staging IP ranges and a read-only snapshot VM for non-invasive scans. We'll push to keep the language that any destructive testing (e.g., load tests, chaos testing) requires prior written approval and a separate addendum.
- Evidence cadence: SOC 2 artifact bundle quarterly is fine; 30-day SLA for evidence is tight but achievable if the request maps to a defined artifact list. Suggest we enumerate the list (e.g., latest SOC 2 report, pen-test summary, architecture diagram, key rotation policy PDF). For ad-hoc logs/traces we should retain the right to negotiate a scoped scope/timebox if high volume is requested.

I'll attach the pen-test SLA table and a sample artifact manifest for Laura to reference.

Ben

Thanks team — drafting precise redline language below we can send to Coventis. Key commercial/legal considerations included. Please flag if anything is unacceptable.

Suggested redline (to insert into Security Exhibit / Audit Rights section):

"Security Exhibit — Audit Rights and Penetration Testing"
1. Penetration Testing: Customer may request a penetration test subject to the following: (i) Customer shall provide a request detailing scope and objectives at least fourteen (14) days prior to any non-production test and at least six (6) weeks prior to any production-impacting or full-scope test; (ii) Redwood shall provide ephemeral staging IP ranges and may, at its discretion, provide a read-only snapshot for non-destructive testing; (iii) Destructive testing (including but not limited to load, availability or chaos engineering) requires prior written approval and a separate addendum addressing risk allocation.

2. Evidence and Artifact Requests: Redwood will make the following artifacts available to Customer on a quarterly basis: (a) latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted as needed), (b) executive summary of most recent penetration test, (c) system architecture diagram, (d) change-control and key-rotation policies. For ad-hoc evidence requests, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide requested artifacts within thirty (30) calendar days if the request maps to the artifact manifest; log-level or high-volume extraction requests will be subject to scope and fees and a mutually agreed timebox. Escalation: if evidence is not provided within thirty (30) days, Customer may escalate to Redwood's Head of Security for resolution.

3. Dedicated Capacity: If the Order Form references "Dedicated" capacity, Redwood confirms single-tenant logical isolation per the captioned Order Form. Physical co-tenancy of hardware is permitted; logical tenancy and customer-specific encryption keys (KMS) will be used to enforce data separation.

4. Confidentiality & Evidence Handling: All exchanged evidence shall be marked "Confidential" and treated per the Confidentiality section. Customer may not publicly disclose raw penetration test findings without Redwood's prior written consent.

Action items:
- Karthik: confirm whether we want a hard 30-day SLA or "commercially reasonable efforts" language tied to artifact manifest.
- Ben: confirm the artifact manifest names/formats and that pen-test summary redaction guidance is acceptable.
- Markus: OK to send to Arjun with attachments and the redlined exhibit?

Laura

Laura Bennett | Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Arjun — thanks for the clear asks and the procurement checklist. Internal team reviewed and we can commit to the below redlines; attaching a marked-up Security Exhibit and an updated order form for your procurement review. Highlights: 

- Pen-test scheduling: non-production tests: 14 days notice; production-impacting or full-scope tests: 6–8 week scheduling window. Destructive testing requires a signed addendum.
- Evidence cadence and SLA: Redwood will provide a quarterly SOC 2 artifact bundle and will accept ad-hoc artifact requests; for any request that maps to our artifact manifest we'll provide the material within thirty (30) calendar days. Log-level/high-volume extractions will be scoped and may incur fees. If the 30-day window is missed, escalation route is to Ben Carter (Head of Security).
- Dedicated capacity: confirmed single-tenant logical isolation; order form updated to call this out explicitly.

Attachments: Coventis_OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf (redlines), pen-test-sla-table.xlsx

Next steps: If that aligns with Coventis' procurement policy we'll ask for countersign by 10/30 to keep the implemented go-live timeline. Happy to take a 20 minute call tomorrow if you prefer to walk through the redlines.

Best,
Markus Klein
